extracted.intended_audience: Authors and mathematicians typesetting displayed mathematics and commutative diagrams using AMS-LaTeX and XY-pic
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing aligned multi-line mathematical displays, controlling equation numbers/tags, and drawing commutative diagrams with the XY-pic package in AMS-LaTeX. Covers selection and usage of environments (align, aligned, gathered, alignat, flalign, cases, etc.), spacing and vertical alignment options, and XY-pic node/arrow/label techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use align / align* for displays with a single alignment point
rubrics_metrics.description: To display several lines of mathematics with horizontal alignment, use the align environment (align* omits equation numbers). Lines are separated by \\ and each line has an ampersand & immediately preceding the symbol to be aligned with the corresponding symbols on the other lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can place \label inside lines and cross-reference them (e.g., see \eqref{...}). Examples show two-line aligned displays producing numbered equations. Both align and align* allow multiple columns (see 7.5.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: aligned and split for alignment inside a larger display
rubrics_metrics.description: The aligned environment does not create a display of its own but allows several lines of mathematics with alignment (as in align*) to be used inside another displayed mathematics environment. The split environment is similar but lacks some options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: aligned doesn’t produce equation numbers; if the enclosing display produces a number that number is vertically centered unless aligned uses the optional argument [t] or [b]. Split can always be replaced by aligned; aligned has options (vertical alignment [t]/[b], multiple alignment points) not possible with split.

rubrics_metrics.name: gathered for centered lines inside a larger display
rubrics_metrics.description: The gathered environment does not create a display of its own; it allows several lines of mathematics, each centered as in gather, to be used inside a displayed mathematics environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gathered can take optional argument [t] or [b] to control vertical alignment when used inside a larger display (so the equation number or surrounding material aligns to top/bottom instead of centered). Use gathered inside equation to give one equation number to the whole block.

rubrics_metrics.name: align/align* support multiple columns (multiple alignment points)
rubrics_metrics.description: The align and align* environments (and aligned) can create displays where each line is broken into several pieces, with each piece horizontally aligned at a chosen character—i.e., multiple columns with alignment within each column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When typing this, lines are separated by \\, different displays on each line are separated by &, and symbols to be aligned are preceded by &. For an alignment with n columns, each line will have at most 2n-1 ampersands. If you want explicit control over spacing between columns, use alignat.

rubrics_metrics.name: flalign / flalign* to push outer columns to margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the flalign (or flalign* to omit numbers) environment to produce alignments like multiple columns but with the leftmost column flush left and the rightmost column flush right, placing outermost aligned blocks flush against the margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax mirrors align but the layout forces outer columns to the page margins. Useful for wide multi-column displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: alignat / alignat* for chosen spacing between columns
rubrics_metrics.description: alignat (and alignat*) produce alignments with multiple alignment points but do not insert horizontal space between columns, so you can insert the exact amount of space you want.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: alignat requires an argument specifying the number of columns. Insert spacing (e.g., \qquad) at the beginning of one column to make that space appear in all rows; it suffices to insert the space in a single row because alignment forces it to appear in all rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: alignedat for chosen spacing inside larger displays
rubrics_metrics.description: The alignedat environment is like aligned (used as part of a larger display) but allows you to choose the spacing between columns; it does not insert inter-column space and has a required argument for the number of columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alignedat when you need precise column spacing for an aligned subblock that is itself inside another display (e.g., inside equation or a brace construct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional vertical alignment [t] or [b] for aligned/gathered blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: When aligned (or gathered or alignedat) is used as part of a display involving other elements, by default it is vertically aligned at its center. The environment can take an optional argument of [t] or [b] to cause vertical alignment at the top or bottom row.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use [t] to align the top rows, [b] to align bottom rows; examples (7.8) and (7.9) illustrate differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cases environment for piecewise definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The cases environment constructs the usual display of several cases and is used as part of a displayed mathematics environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inside cases use & to separate the expression and the condition: e.g., \begin{cases} x & \text{if $x\ge0$} \\ -x & \text{if $x<0$} \end{cases}. Also usable inside align/gather contexts; see examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce one equation number for multi-line displays
rubrics_metrics.description: To have multiple lines with horizontal alignment but only one equation number, use the equation environment to produce the number and put an aligned environment (or gathered for centered lines) inside it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equation + aligned to both align horizontally and get a single number for the whole block; use equation + gathered to have centered lines and a single number. Use alignedat if you need exact inter-column spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress individual line numbers with \notag
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want equation numbers on some but not all lines, use an environment that numbers every line and then suppress particular line numbers by typing \notag at the end of those lines (before \\ or at the end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows using \notag on first and third lines while leaving labels on others. This works in environments like align that ordinarily number lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Override equation numbers with \tag and \tag*
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands \tag{stuff} and \tag*{stuff} allow you to override normal equation numbering for any line: \tag inserts 'stuff' enclosed in parentheses; \tag* inserts 'stuff' as-is (no added parentheses). They work even in normally unnumbered displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place \tag or \tag* at the end of the line. If you want parentheses included in cross-references, consider using \tag* and include parentheses in the tag text itself (example \tag*{$(*)$}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include XY-pic with \usepackage[all,cmtip]{xy} and \xymatrix syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: To draw commutative diagrams include \usepackage[all,cmtip]{xy} and (optionally) \let\objectstyle=\displaystyle. Create diagrams with \xymatrix followed by braces describing a rectangular array of nodes (nodes separated by &, rows by \\).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enclose nodes in braces {} (safe practice). A node should not begin with a macro or an asterisk. Arrows are specified immediately following the source node using \ar[target] where target is r, l, d, u, rr, dr, etc. Many examples illustrate basic 2×2 diagrams and omitted nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center equation numbers vertically relative to diagrams with \vcenter
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’d like the equation number to be centered vertically with respect to the diagram, enclose the \xymatrix command in a \vcenter when placing it in an equation environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrap the entire \xymatrix in \vcenter{ ... } inside equation to vertically center the displayed number (example (8.2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit nodes by using & or \\ appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all nodes need appear in a diagram. To omit a node in the middle of a row, include the & that moves to the next node; to omit a node at end of a row, end the row with \\ and continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show diagrams with missing nodes producing irregular grids; arrows may still be specified to skip columns (e.g., \ar[rr]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change row/column spacing with @=, @R=, @C=
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert spacing commands immediately after \xymatrix and before the left brace: @=dimen to set both row and column spacing, @R=dimen to set row spacing, @C=dimen to set column spacing. Dimen can be positive, zero, or negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer ex for vertical distances and em for horizontal so spacing adapts to font size. Negative column spacing can be useful for diagrams that otherwise would not fit; examples show @C=-12em for very wide nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift nodes sideways with *+[r]{...} and *+[l]{...}
rubrics_metrics.description: You can shift a node right by enclosing it in braces preceded by *+[r] and shift left with *+[l].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this when you want the arrows to point to a portion (like a name) but display a wider node (like a definition). Note large shifted nodes can increase column spacing; counteract via @C negative values or adjust spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create arrows that pass under nodes (segmented arrows)
rubrics_metrics.description: To create an arrow that passes under a sequence of nodes and then goes on, follow \ar by ’[node] for each node you pass under, followed by [finalnode]. Using an empty node as an intermediate allows crossing effects where one arrow passes under another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples use \ar ’[r] ’[rr] [rrr] to pass under B and continue to D. Useful for complex crossing and segmented arrows; see sections 8.4 and 8.5.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label arrows with ^{...} and _{...}, center labels with - and place at arbitrary points
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a label above an arrow with ^{thelabel} and below with _{thelabel}. To center a label along the arrow (rather than halfway between node centers) insert a - immediately after ^ or _. To place a label at an arbitrary fraction a between 0 and 1 from source to target, use ^(a){label} or _(a){label}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \ar[r]^{f} (default halfway between centers), \ar[r]^-{f} (centered on arrow), \ar[r]^(.3){f} (30% along arrow). Use these to fine-tune label placement when sources/targets have differing sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label each segment of a segmented arrow
rubrics_metrics.description: For segmented arrows created with the ' (pass-under) notation, attach a label to each segment by supplying a ^{...} (or _{...}) after each segment specifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \ar ’[r]^{f} ’[rr]^{g} [rrr]^{h} produces three labeled segments f,g,h on the arrow from A to D with intermediate passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break an arrow with a label using | and position the breaking label
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the vertical bar | in place of ^ or _ to have the label 'break' the arrow. The break-label can be positioned anywhere along the arrow using centering (-) or fractional placement (e.g., |(.7){m}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \ar[r]|{f} makes the label interrupt the arrow; combine with fractional placement to position the hole/label precisely. Useful to create visual gaps or to have one arrow pass over another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make one arrow cross over another by creating a hole (\hole) and precise positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a gap in the second arrow at the crossing spot by breaking that arrow with the special label \hole (e.g., \ar[dr]|{\hole}). To position the hole precisely, instead of a fraction use !{[node1];[node2]} to denote the point where the straight line from [node1] to [node2] crosses the arrow (works for straight arrows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show \ar[urr]|(.33){\hole} or \ar[urr]|!{[u];[r]}{\hole}. This produces a hole so the other arrow appears to cross over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make room for large labels by enlarging diagram or adding empty columns
rubrics_metrics.description: XY-pic ignores arrow label sizes when constructing diagrams, so a large label may overwrite nodes. You can enlarge the entire diagram using spacing commands (@C/@R/@=) or create an extra empty column/row (or put an \hspace into an empty node) to make room for the label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use \xymatrix@C=6em{...} to enlarge, or insert an extra column of empty nodes and use \ar[rr] for arrows spanning the empty column; optionally insert \hspace{3em} into an empty node to expand space without enlarging whole diagram.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use many arrow styles via \ar@{...} notation
rubrics_metrics.description: XY-pic supports a wide variety of arrow shaft/tail/head styles expressed by \ar@{...} (e.g., @{.>}, @{-->}, @{=>}, @{->>}, @{<->}, @{|->}, @{^{(}->}, @{=}, @{.}, @{-->>}, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 lists common arrow styles; you can omit head/tail or make arrows invisible (\ar@{}). Mix and match styles to indicate different morphism types or relations; examples demonstrate dotted, dashed, double-headed, hook arrows, monomorphisms, epimorphisms, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invisible arrows for placing items outside grid
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \ar@{} (an invisible arrow) to create placements or alignment effects without drawing an arrow, useful for placing things outside the node grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined with node omission and spacing controls, invisible arrows let you position text or objects in arbitrary diagram locations while preserving placement logic.
